label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, C, B, D where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Upright open-ended cylinder with straight sides, a slight rim flare at top and bottom, and a flat bottom, as a 55-gallon drum reads in all six side views and the front-left/front-right/back-left/back-right views. No part sticks out except the two bungs on the lid, which a drum has.

M2.reason: Measured 23.2 x 23.2 x 35.5. Asked: 23 across and 34 high. Across is 0.9% over, height 4.4% over, both within 10%.

M3.reason: The brief asks for a drum, rusted, with a hazard stripe. Present: the cylindrical body, a lid on top with two bungs (visible in the top view), a flat bottom (below view), two hoop rings on the side (front view), and the yellow and black diagonal stripe on the upper band. The stripe is painted on, as Valve paints such bands. Nothing asked is missing.

M4.reason: Rust-brown painted metal over the body and lid, with orange-brown highlights on the hoops and rim. Yellow and black hazard stripe on the band, as the brief asks. Colours agree across all ten views and read as one material.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe is crisp and diagonal on every side, the rust mottling is present across the body and lid, and the hoops and rims carry their light edge highlights. The surface reads at a sharpness close to Half-Life's own drums.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric for this line-up. Measured: in four readings in four orders, the judges did not pick the asset as the odd one out in a way that identifies it; it passed for one of the game's three props beside them.

M7.reason: Stands upright on a flat bottom in the side and below views. The lid is on top, as the rim and bungs show. A drum has no front to face, so the front reads as correct.

M8.reason: SMAK check: no errors. 336 triangles, under the 422 that the most-spent Valve prop of this kind and size uses, and no more than the rule allows. It is above the third-quartile warning of 156 but below the failing bar. Top, bottom and sides are closed in every view; nothing open or floating.
